thread:
anika: Quick sync — I'm updating the benchmark spec for kernel selection + KV-cache interactions. We need a single canonical definition for TTFT and TPOT so replay vs synthetic runs are comparable. TL;DR: propose changes below.

ben: Nice — can you spell out the defs you want to lock? people iterate on wording a lot.

anika: Sure. Proposed defs: 
- TTFT (Time to First Token): time from request ingress (server recv) to first token byte sent to client. includes routing + kernel startup + kv lookup if on critical path.
- TPOT (Tokens Produced Over Time): measured as tokens/sec after first token, averaged over the steady-state period (exclude the initial 500ms warmup window).
- p95/p99: latency percentiles measured on TTFT for user-facing SLOs; for tail analysis we also calculate token-emission p95 over sample windows.
- Goodput vs QPS: QPS = number of requests accepted/sec. Goodput = number of tokens successfully delivered within SLO per second (so failed/timeouts and responses past SLO don't count).

chao: +1 on TTFT wording. For KV cache we need to be explicit: TTFT_cold vs TTFT_warm. Cold = no prefix hits (KV miss), Warm = prefix hit before request arrives. We'll also track cache_hit_ratio per route.

anika: Good call. Add these to the spec: record a binary kv_prefix_hit flag and cache_age histogram (ms since last write).

daria: On batching heuristics: we should run two canonical modes in the harness: (1) token-limited batching (batch until token budget or max latency), (2) request-limited batching (batch up to N requests). Many regressions only show up in token-limited mode.

ben: Do we have a reproducible command for the replay harness that sets these modes? we should embed it in the spec so CI runs the same experiments.

anika: Yes — example: 
```
# replay harness example (linux)
./replay_harness --profile=canonical-chat --mode=token-limited --token-budget=4096 --max-latency-ms=200 --warmup-requests=2000 --measure-window=30000
```
That sets a 30s measure window after warmup. 

profiling-bot: CPU: 58% on kernel-selector, GPU mem: 74% on model, mean kv_lookup 1.9ms, kernel-switch overhead 3.4ms (sample). Trace: /traces/1864123456/profile-1

ella: FYI we saw a regression on branch feature/batch-bump: TTFT p95 jumped from 110ms -> 210ms on synthetic-short prompts in token-limited mode. It only reproes when kv_prefix_hit ratio ~0.2. Might be kernel-selection thrash.

chao: That pattern suggests frequent kernel-switch calls because batch composition flips between short and long sequences. If KV hits reduce effective seq len but kernel decision still picks long-kernel, we pay penalty. We should instrument: kernel_decision_reason and batch_seq_len_variance.

anika: Agreed. New required telemetry fields for experiments: kernel_choice, kernel_decision_reason, batch_seq_len_mean, batch_seq_len_stddev, kv_prefix_hit, kv_prefix_age_ms. Add them to the JSON metrics output.

ben: For apples-to-apples comparisons, the spec must require: same hardware image, same model weights + quantization, same routing policy, identical traffic profile (seq length distribution + arrival process), and matching cache precondition (seed cache state).

daria: About cache precondition — we need two canonical cache states: cold (empty), warm (seeded with canonical prefixes from training set, hit ratio ~0.6). Provide a seeding tool in harness.

anika: I'll add a `--cache-seed-file` flag to the harness and a small generator. Example command: `./replay_harness --seed-cache=canonical_seeds.json --target-hit=0.6`

ella: For regressions, let's standardize the regression signal: 
- Primary: TTFT_p95 increase > 20% AND TPOT decrease > 10% in the same run.
- Secondary: Goodput drop > 5% or p99 TTFT increase > 15%.
If primary triggers, auto-open perf-incident with attached traces.

profiling-bot: regression-alert: run 1864123456 feature/batch-bump TTFT_p95 +91% TPOT -12% traces uploaded -> /incidents/1864123456-batch-bump

ben: One more practical: when comparing replay vs synthetic, always match the inter-arrival-time distribution. Synthetic uniform arrivals give different batching behavior than Poisson/replay. We'll add three canonical arrival profiles: uniform(steady), poisson(lambda), and bursty (heavy-tailed inter-arrival).

chao: Also add a short test that sweeps batch parameters to find knee points: token_budget = [512, 1024, 2048, 4096], max_latency = [50,100,200,400]. Collect TPOT and goodput heatmaps.

anika: Action items: 
1) I'll update benchmark spec with exact telemetry fields + definitions (PR by EOD).
2) chao/daria: add kernel_decision_reason + batch stats to harness and seed-cache tool (this week).
3) ben/ella: run regression suite on feature/batch-bump and attach traces.
4) infra: please pin hardware image and publish canonical seed file to /bench/canonical.

ben: Sounds good. Thanks — brief follow-ups only in thread. :thumbsup:

anika: Thanks all — will open PR and link back here.
